text: Create `docs/docs/developers/apiease-public-api.md` for the APIEase public API.
goal:
Implement a new top-level Developers documentation area in this Docusaurus repository and populate it with initial documentation for the APIEase public API, apiease-cli, and apiease-template.

Goals

Add a new top-level Developers section to the docs sidebar
Make apiease-template the primary developer entry point
Do not create separate top-level quickstarts for the public API or apiease-cli
Keep existing Requests, Functions, Variables, Widgets, and General sections intact
Cross-link to existing conceptual docs instead of duplicating request concepts that already exist in the current docs
Target documentation structure

Developers
Developer overview
Why use the template
Quickstart with apiease-template
Using APIEase with AI agents
APIEase public API
apiease-cli
apiease-template
Documentation expectations

The template quickstart should be the canonical start here path for developers and AI agents
The quickstart should explain how a user starts from the template, configures auth, uses the CLI from the template repo, versions generated artifacts in git, and syncs or interacts with APIEase through the public API by way of the CLI and template workflow
The public API section should explain the public API as an interface, covering core concepts, auth, request conventions, and the most important developer-facing usage patterns
The apiease-cli section should explain installation, configuration, command usage, and how it fits into the template-based workflow
The apiease-template section should explain the purpose of the template, expected repo layout, artifacts under source control, and the intended developer workflow
The AI agents page should explain how AI agents such as Codex should operate inside the template repo, how they should use the CLI and public API, and how source control fits into that workflow
Do not create separate top-level Workflows or Reference sections unless, during implementation, the content clearly justifies them. Prefer keeping material inside the API, CLI, and template docs unless there is a strong reason to split it out
Research requirements

Reach into ../apiease to understand how the public API works and document it accurately
Reach into ../apiease-cli to understand how apiease-cli works and document it accurately
Reach into ../apiease-template to understand how apiease-template works and document it accurately
If the template directory is actually named ../apiease-tmplate in the local environment, use that actual path, but document the product as apiease-template
Base the new docs on the real code, commands, configuration, and workflows in those sibling repositories rather than inventing behavior
Implementation requirements

Update docs/sidebars.js to add the new Developers section
Create the new markdown or MDX files under docs/docs in a clean Developers-oriented folder structure
Keep headings short, scannable, and consistent with the repository style
Use relative links between docs pages
Prefer concise task-oriented writing for onboarding pages
Link back to existing Requests docs where request concepts are already documented
Avoid duplicating detailed request concept explanations that belong in the existing Requests section
Ensure the new pages build cleanly in Docusaurus
Run the docs build after changes and fix any issues
Quality bar

The new developer docs should feel like a coherent developer entry point, not scattered add-on pages
The template should clearly read as the recommended starting path
The public API and CLI pages should clearly support the template workflow
The AI agent guidance should be explicit enough for Codex-style agents to use the docs effectively
Keep the first implementation practical and high-signal. Favor solid initial coverage over exhaustive reference material if time or context is limited
context: Use `../apiease` as the source of truth for the public API behavior, authentication model, and developer-facing usage patterns.
Reuse existing Requests documentation for request concepts that are already explained elsewhere in this docs site.
steps: Inspect the sibling API repository to identify the real public API surface, auth requirements, request conventions, and the main integration patterns developers need.
Write a concise developer-facing page that explains the public API as an interface used within the broader template and CLI workflow.
Cross-link to the existing Requests section where detailed request concepts already exist.
constraints: Base all documented behavior on the real code and configuration in `../apiease`.
Do not create a separate top-level quickstart for the public API.
Avoid duplicating detailed request concept explanations that belong in the existing Requests docs.
acceptanceCriteria: The page explains what the public API is for, how authentication works, the key request conventions, and the most important developer-facing usage patterns.
The page positions the public API as part of the recommended template and CLI workflow rather than as a separate onboarding track.
The page links to existing Requests docs instead of restating detailed request concepts.
